sex noun

being male or female

also sexes, both sexes, the opposite sex, gender (male or female), gender (grammar)

classical

Cic. Inv. 1.35
Liv. 27.11: ambiguō inter marem ac fēminam sexū īnfantem
Suet. Aug. 31
Traupman 377

sexus, sexūs m.

noun, fourth declension · Declension on Wiktionary

sex, male or female

Of people and animals: virīlis sexus, muliebris or fēmineus sexus; of both sexes, utrīusque sexūs. The grammatical gender of a noun is genus.

Other words

  • secus n. (indeclinable) — sex, in the phrases virīle secus and muliebre secus

    noun, indeclinable, neuter · also used · classical · Liv. 26.47.1

    An old word of the historians, used as an accusative of respect: virīle secus, of the male sex (Lewis & Short).

  • genus, generis n. — gender (in grammar)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 320 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • atque hominum genus et in sexū cōnsīderātur, virīle an muliebre sit

    and in the case of people one considers their sex, whether male or femaleCic. Inv. 1.35

  • juvenēs utrīusque sexūs prohibuit ūllum nocturnum spectāculum frequentāre nisi cum aliquō majōre nātū propinquōrum

    he forbade young people of both sexes to attend any show at night unless with an older relativeSuet. Aug. 31

  • Līberōrum capitum virīle secus ad decem mīlia capta

    about ten thousand free persons of the male sex were takenLiv. 26.47.1

See also male, man, child, sex.
